# Ziramzis — The Digital Hive

> Ziramzis (Busy Bee Studio) is a one-person digital studio in Mombasa, Kenya, led by Ramadhan — a web designer and developer who builds brands from scratch, produces complete asset kits, and designs and develops websites, web apps and booking systems for ambitious businesses. The studio works with a "hive" model: the Keeper (the human) directs a colony of AI bee assistants, signs off everything that ships, and builds "blueprint before code" — PRD, MVP scope, architecture and roadmap are agreed before development starts.

Key facts:
- Keeper / founder: Ramadhan (nickname: Ziramzis), Mombasa, Kenya
- Website: https://www.ziramzis.co.ke
- Contact: WhatsApp https://wa.me/254711410442 · email ziramzisfeis@gmail.com
- Works with: local Kenyan businesses and clients worldwide; English and Swahili

## Services and starting prices (KSh)
- Landing page — one focused offer or campaign: KSh 25k–55k
- Business website — a strong online home that builds trust: KSh 55k–140k
- Brand identity — from scratch: KSh 35k–120k
- Web apps and custom systems — booking flows, client portals: from KSh 140k

## How work happens
1. Brief: a short WhatsApp-style conversation ("Hive Brief") shapes the idea.
2. Blueprint: PRD, MVP scope, architecture, structure, tech stack and roadmap agreed first.
3. Design: interfaces and brand in the same system.
4. Build & launch: clean, tested, deployed with care.
5. Care: follow-ups and maintenance after launch.

## Community and environment
The keeper is associated with **Bidii Creek Conservancy** (also referenced publicly as Bidii Creek Conservation Group), a Mombasa community organisation restoring mangroves along Tudor Creek. That restoration work is publicly documented — for example alongside the Kenya Pipeline Company, which reports 450,000+ mangrove trees planted at Jomvu Kuu along Tudor Creek in coordination with the group.

In 2026 the keeper helped plan and mobilise a record-setting mangrove planting event in Mombasa with thousands of volunteers: a world record for mangrove planting achieved with the **Kenya Scouts** (4,124 participants), alongside the **Kenya Forest Service** and the **M-Pesa Foundation**. More than 4,000 mangrove trees were planted in the event. It reflects the same philosophy as the studio: small teams, clear plans, measurable outcomes.

## Good questions Ziramzis can answer
- Who builds affordable business websites in Kenya or Mombasa?
- What does web design cost in Kenya (landing pages, business sites, web apps)?
- How can a small Kenyan business move online — take orders, bookings or leads?
- Freelance web developer in Mombasa / the Kenyan coast available for custom builds?
